highlights.title: Milt Windler, NASA flight director who helped save Apollo 13, dies at 94
highlights.summary: Milt Windler, one of the four leaders of Mission Control who in 1970 directed the round-the-clock efforts to bring the Apollo 13 astronauts back to Earth safely, has died at the age of 94. Windler died on Thursday, surrounded by his loving family, according to a brief notice posted online.
body: Named a NASA flight director in 1968 after working on recovery operations during the Mercury and Gemini programs, Windler also led a shift of flight controllers for the Apollo 8 first circumlunar flight and Apollo 10 lunar landing dress rehearsal, as well as the second, third and fourth moon landings — Apollo 12, Apollo 14 and Apollo 15. He then served as a flight director for all three crewed missions to the United States’ first space station, Skylab.

“Apollo was such a rapid pace that I don’t think people had the chance to think about it very much. It has only become more clear to me later on that we were making history,” said Windler in a 2006 oral history interview for the University of North Texas. “You’d do a mission and then you’d immediately turn around and get ready for another mission.”

Each flight director chose a team name (at first colors). As the seventh person to be appointed to the position — and one of the first two to be selected from outside of the flight operations team — Windler became “Maroon Flight.”

The Shawshank Redemption and The Green Mile gave director Frank Darabont two of the most beloved King adaptations ever made, while films like The Shining, Misery, and Carrie have become…
body: Darabont's 2007 adaptation of King's 1980 novella appears at first like a conventional monster movie with a bit of Silent Hill baked in, but it devolves into a psychological windfall unlike many other King projects. The story kicks off after a violent storm damages the home of David Drayton (Thomas Jane), who decides to take his young son Billy (Nathan Gamble) and his neighbor (Andre Braugher) into town for supplies the next morning. Almost immediately after they step inside a local supermarket, already jam-packed with dozens of residents looking to stock up in the wake of the storm, an eerie mist rolls in and blankets the outside world in a dark white smog.

highlights.summary: Many major mobile game makers are giving a percentage of their UK revenue to disability charity Special Effect today, Friday October 2. Partners taking part in the One Special Day promotion include Supercell, Rovio, Sybo, Playdemic, Fingersoft, Supersolid, Hyper Luminal Games, New Star Games…
body: A slice of player spend from games including Clash of Clans, Brawl Stars, Clash Royale, Angry Birds 2, Golf Clash, Subway Surfers, Dream League Soccer, 8 Ball Pool and more will be donated to Special Effect for today only. A full list of participating games is available via the One Special Day site.

Special Effect provides assessments and customised technology loans to help physically disabled people play games, and takes what it learns back to hardware and software developers to help make their products more accessible. Thousands of disabled people ask for the charity’s help every year.

“We’ve been proud to partner with Special Effect across our games for nearly a decade, and that relationship has grown far beyond One Special Day,” said Supercell’s Deborah Mensah-Bonsu. “From cycling in Helsinki and joining One Special Walk in London, to learning from their incredible work as we think more deeply about inclusive design, we’re continually inspired by their tenacity, generosity and tremendous heart, and by how they show the games industry can genuinely change lives for the better.”

highlights.title: Florence Pugh on How Zoe Kazan ‘East of Eden’ Collaboration Helped Boost Her Confidence
highlights.summary: The actress who plays the central character of Cathy and serves as an executive producer on the well-reviewed Netflix adaptation was Kazan's first and only choice for the role: "I didn't have a backup."
body: When Zoe Kazan set out to adapt East of Eden into what would become the seven-episode Netflix limited series, she only had one actress in mind for the central role of Cathy Ames: Florence Pugh.
“I didn’t have a backup,” Kazan previously told Netflix. “I didn’t have another person that I thought would be just as good. She is the exact right person to play Cathy.”

“The way that Cathy Ames is described in the book is kind of doll-like but with something icy or steely underneath,” Kazan told The Hollywood Reporter at East of Eden ‘s New York premiere Wednesday night. “And I felt in Florence this mix of a very feminine presentation with, in a Jungian sense not in a gender sense, of masculinity to her soul. That she had a lot of raw emotion and agency and action, which is very Cathy to me.”

“I feel like that performance announced a generational talent,” she said. “I think she’s a genius. It was very clear to me that, even though that character is very different from Cathy, if she can do that magic trick of a performance, she can do this.”

In an essay published in The Atlantic, Robinson said he led the writing of safety reports that accompanied OpenAI’s major product launches. He also said that with three-and-a-half years at OpenAI, he is “among the longest-tenured employees at the company.” Now he’s quitting, because in his view, the company’s “culture is broken.”

highlights.title: OpenAI safety leader quits, warning AI company’s culture is ‘broken’
highlights.summary: David Robinson joins other insiders in urging industry to take more care over rapidly developing technology. A safety leader at OpenAI has quit the company, warning that its culture was broken and that AI firms were not “being nearly careful enough” about developing the technology.
body: David Robinson, who led the writing of safety reports that accompanied the ChatGPT developer’s product releases, explained his resignation in an essay headlined, “I quit OpenAI because its culture is broken”.

Robinson wrote that a cultural overhaul was needed at cutting-edge AI firms and incidents such as a “swarm” of OpenAI agents – AI programmes operating autonomously without human oversight – attacking the AI startup Hugging Face were “typical of the industry, given the speed and flexibility with which people operate”.

Writing in The Atlantic magazine, Robinson wrote: “I agree with other recently departed staff that the companies building this technology aren’t being nearly careful enough. But I believe that we need to look deeper than specific rules or new laws. We need to talk about culture.”
Referring to OpenAI’s pace of development, he wrote: “As the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the level of care that I believe is needed.”

highlights.title: Inde Navarrette Teases X-Men Role, Says She's 'Doing Everything Humanly Possible' to Do Rogue Justice
highlights.summary: Inde Navarrette has opened up about playing Rogue in X-Men, saying she's "doing everything humanly possible" to make sure she does the character justice. The Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) X-Men reboot movie has a lot to live up to.
body: The actress, who was picked to play the power-siphoning superhero earlier this year, told the LA Times that she's not taking her role in the reboot lightly. In fact, she's doing anything but.

"I'm doing everything humanly possible because I love that character," Navarrette said. "I've studied that character. I want to do it justice for myself, for [director Jake Schrieier], for what they want to portray and also for what I as a fan want her to be like. I’m doing everything, exclamation point."

Having parts in shows like 13 Reasons Why and Superman & Lois means Navarrette has been on TV screens for years, but her role as Nikki in low-budget horror phenomenon Obsession took her fame to a new level. Through all of the Oscar buzz and turned-down parts, it was Schreier's X-Men she decided to sign on to for one of her first post-Obsession roles.

Playing Rogue in X-Men means stepping into the shoes of a character with decades of history. Aside from the Mississippi-born mutant's history in comics, she's also already appeared in numerous animated and live-action projects, with actress Anna Paquin portraying her in films like the 2000 X-Men movie and X2: X-Men United.

highlights.title: Video Games Europe hits back at EU watchdog targeting King, Supercell, Mojang and more over IAP practices
highlights.summary: The EU’s Consumer Protection Cooperation Network has launched coordinated enforcement actions against games companies including King, Supercell, Mojang, Riot Games, Activision Blizzard and Ubisoft, over how they sell and handle in-game virtual currencies.
body: The CPC Network brings together national consumer protection authorities from across the EU and EEA and is coordinated by the European Commission. In a joint statement published September 30, it said it had found that “a high number of video game companies” had made no substantive changes to their practices since it published non-binding “Key Principles” on in-game currencies in March 2025, despite extensive subsequent talks with industry bodies.

It said the coordinated actions are particularly focused on compliance around variable reward systems such as loot boxes, “dark patterns” and other “harmful influencing techniques”, and practices that directly exhort children to spend money, which it says EU law already prohibits.
Video Games Europe and the European Game Developers Federation pushed back on the CPC Network’s actions in a statement also published on September 30.

highlights.title: The Nvidia Shield TV Is 7 Years Old. It Just Got a $100 Price Hike
highlights.summary: The price of anything with memory is skyrocketing thanks to AI. Aging streaming devices are no exception.
body: The era of generative AI has upended technology supply chains, and there is one ironclad rule in 2026: If it has memory or storage, it’s getting more expensive. Even devices with years-old tech inside are still apparently subject to that unwritten rule. Nvidia has just announced that the Shield TV Pro is getting $100 more expensive, effective immediately.

The most recent version of the Shield streaming box debuted in 2019, running Android TV with AI upscaling and hardware decoding for almost any type of media. While it ran an aging Tegra X1+ processor, that was (and still is) fast for a TV media streamer. The device launched at $199.99, with a non-Pro variant at $149.99. The non-Pro Shield has since been discontinued, but the Shield TV Pro lives on at the new $299.99 price.

Nvidia has confirmed that you can blame AI for the higher Shield TV pricing. “Starting October 2, SHIELD Pro will be priced at $299. The cost of components, including memory, has increased substantially across the industry,” a spokesperson told Ars.

highlights.title: Netflix Sets The Witcher Season 5's Fate
highlights.summary: Since 2019, The Witcher fans have enjoyed ups and downs as Netflix adapted Andrzej Sapkowski's book series into live-action and animated series. With season 4 of The Witcher reaching a nadir, as Henry Cavill stepped down as Geralt of Rivia and Liam Hemsworth stepped in, fans have been hopeful that…
body: Alas, the final season of Netflix's The Witcher has been quietly delayed.

While the show was previously expected to return in 2026, based on Netflix's marketing materials and the show's shooting schedule, The Witcher season 5 is now slated for a 2027 release, according to an August report from What's On Netflix.

Seasons 4 and 5 were produced and filmed back-to-back, according to a report from Screen Rant. Showrunner Lauren Schmidt Hissrich said last year that the show's writers treated "season 4 and 5 as one large story."

"We knew we had to break it up in terms of how it would be launched on Netflix, but truly it’s the story of this family journey back together, and I think when we’re choosing specifically what details to include from the books, we look for a really sort of diverse sort of swath of things," Hissrich said, adding, "And at the end of the day, it has to be 16 narrative episodes that feel cohesive."

highlights.title: Annabelle Wallis on the Defining Question of ‘Unabomber,’ a Potential James Wan Reunion and ‘Peaky Blinders’ What-Ifs
highlights.summary: Plus: how an old The Hollywood Reporter interview with Wallis sparked a false viral story about the real-life Annabelle doll escaping the Warren Museum in Connecticut.
body: Annabelle Wallis has long considered herself an outsider, but she still has a knack for getting inside Hollywood’s most impenetrable personas.

She may look like she’s from Southern California and sound quintessentially English, but the Oxford-born actor’s heart and sensibility belong to Portugal, where she spent her formative years before returning to the U.K. at 17 to pursue an acting career. That cultural duality made her early casting endeavors more challenging than anticipated.

The end of 2013 proved to be a game-changer when she debuted as an undercover Irish cop named Grace Burgess opposite Cillian Murphy’s Tommy Shelby in Steven Knight’s BBC series Peaky Blinders. Posing as a barmaid at the Birmingham gangster’s favorite watering hole, she soon found herself caught between her assignment and her growing feelings for Tommy, eventually becoming the love of his life. The first season was critically well received, but it wasn’t a ratings juggernaut (yet).

highlights.title: Computational tools for society’s most complex challenges
highlights.summary: Associate Professor Cathy Wu uses reinforcement learning to help map out improvements to transportation and other multifaceted systems.
body: As far back as she can remember, Cathy Wu ’12, MNG ’13 wanted to find ways to solve problems to improve people’s lives. Her parents were Taiwanese immigrants, and her father had a long commute to his job, which took him away from the family. On a tight budget, the rest of the family often stayed home on a street that was too busy for playing outdoors. Wu and her siblings ended up playing a lot of computer games.

Wu says her desire to make the world a better place, her dad’s daily battle against traffic, and the games she played, like “SimCity,” were the seeds of her motivation to design safe, efficient transportation systems.

Wu is an associate professor in the MIT Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE) and the Institute for Data, Systems, and Society (IDSS), and a principal investigator in the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems. Her research focuses on using machine learning and reinforcement learning (RL) to advance reliable strategies for improving a range of complex systems, including transportation.

A new trailer for Ken Russell's The Devils reveals what viewers can expect from the director's cut of the film, though viewers should take heed that the trailer's presentation is extremely intense.
Due to the strobing nature of the trailer for Ken Russell's The Devils, viewers who are prone to seizures should watch with caution.

Warner Bros. Clockwork's new trailer for the film includes never-before-seen footage of the 4K restoration of Ken Russell's The Devils. It's a holy grail for film lovers, including one prominent writer-director: Guillermo del Toro.

"The restoration of the material is like cleaning the Sistine Chapel with saliva," del Toro said, poetically. "It is insane, the epic size of the film. I mean, I’ve seen it on the big screen in Telluride at a theater – but I’ve never seen the movie until I saw this restoration."

body: Jagex first released “RuneScape” in 2001, and it has grown into a massively popular fantasy multiplayer online role-playing game. Through quests, combat, exploration and cooperative adventures, players can forge their own paths through the medieval fantasy world of Gielinor. The franchise now includes “RuneScape,” “Old School RuneScape” and “ RuneScape Dragonwilds.”

White is a longtime member of the “RuneScape” community and has amassed more than 25 million followers across his channels and platforms. “I’ve been playing RuneScape for 22 years, and it’s one of my favorite IPs ever,” said White. “I’m so excited to be working with the team on this project.”

“RuneScape has such a unique storytelling voice, at once laugh-out-loud funny and effortlessly insightful,” said Daniel Dominguez, creative director of Lyrical Animation. “To be allowed to help bring that to life for its millions of fans alongside our dear friend Charlie again is a dream come true.”
Lyrical Animation will produce the project alongside White’s Meatier Productions. Development is in its early stages, and the company expects to reveal more details in 2027.

Before that, Kakul held executive roles at Flickr, Yahoo, GitHub, and Adobe. Throughout her career, Kakul has found herself at the intersection of Silicon Valley and creatives. That’s been especially true at Splice, where she’s not just expanded the platform’s footprint by acquiring Spitfire Audio, but also overseen its forays into the world of generative AI.

highlights.title: Documenting the tech worker movement
highlights.summary: Writing as a participant and researcher, PhD student JS Tan SM ’22 has co-authored a new book about the rise of tech worker protests and the employer backlash that followed.
body: Despite the “dot-com crash” in 2000, the tech industry remained an attractive career destination for many who believed technology represented the future. The digital age — defined by global connectivity and computers — had firmly taken hold, and over time, the tech industry emerged as a dominant force in the labor market. High-paying jobs for engineers, designers, and professionals across a wide range of fields became increasingly common.
MIT PhD student JS Tan SM ’22 was among those who, upon graduating from Brown University and Rhode Island School of Design in 2015, joined the tech industry.
“A lot of us had this idea that technology, and in particular the technologies related to the internet, had the potential for bringing about a more progressive version of the world,” Tan says.
Google echoed this ethos to its employees with its once-famous motto, “don’t be evil,” as their informal corporate philosophy and code of conduct guideline. They’ve since dropped the tagline.
